Pathway-centric mapping of differentially enriched proteins in the presynaptic and postsynaptic terminals following methamphetamine (Meth) exposure

Pathway-centric mapping of differentially enriched proteins in the presynaptic and postsynaptic terminals following methamphetamine (Meth) exposure. The proteomic data were overlaid onto a schematic of canonical synaptic processes and cellular components, including dopamine biosynthesis and packaging, the synaptic vesicle cycle, mitochondrial energy metabolism, proteasome-mediated protein degradation, and endoplasmic reticulum organization. The proteins with significant enrichment in Meth-treated samples are highlighted in green, while those reduced are in purple. Proteins lacking a significant concentration change detected are in gray. The node labels indicate gene names. These depictions reflect changes in protein abundance rather than direct measurements of neurotransmitter concentrations. Gene names are provided in the text or Table S2. Key: DA, dopamine; ER, endoplasmic reticulum; TCA, tricarboxylic acid cycle

Deep Proteome Profiling of Rat Dorsal Striatal Synaptoneurosomes Following Methamphetamine Exposure (2026) Laura G. Rodriguez, et al. ACS Chem Neurosci. 2026 Jan 07;17(1). Figure: F5.
